newsitem.title: USA: Conference Bd Q1 business confidence index at 57.
newsitem.headline: Conference Bd Q1 business confidence index at 57.

text.p: Confidence among top U.S. executives continued to rise in the first quarter as the Conference Board's Measure of Business Confidence rose to its highest level in more than two and a half years.
The index rose to 57 in the first quarter, up from 54 in the 1996 fourth quarter and 53 in the 1996 third quarter.
The last time the index had been so high was when it reached 59 in the third quarter of 1994.
A reading above 50 reflects more positive than negative responses from buisness leaders, according to the Conference Board.
Among industries, CEOs in wholesale and retail trade reported the largest improvement in business conditions. Banking and finance deteriorated.
The report found that more than 30 percent of executives plan to hire additional workers during the upcoming year, up significantly from the 10 percent figure seen a year ago.
About 10 percent said they would decrease their workforce, down from 45 percent a year ago.
CEOs said wage and salary costs and other benefits are not major obstacles to hiring more workers. Regulations and litigation, and health care costs were cited as the largest hiring obstacles.
